title: Thirty-One Mornings of Light
subtitle: A Visual Devotional Journey with the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit
selectionRule: Ten polished days from each devotional volume, followed by one new trinitarian culmination.

movements.title: Awakening
movements.promise: The soul wakes to the Father's love.

movements.title: Depths
movements.promise: The heart discovers that Jesus meets and carries us in deep water.

movements.title: Wonders
movements.promise: The road with Jesus opens into the Spirit's living wonder.

movements.title: Kingdom Light
movements.promise: The Spirit fills ordinary lives until the love of God becomes visible.

days.reason: Lady D opens the journey with honest pain held inside the Father's promise.
Lady D's authored Exodus 15:4 calibration day anchors the whole voice standard.
The Father's love moves before performance and gives the visual journey its foundation.
The Father answers relationship before explanation, a strong invitation into trust.
Reconciliation becomes visible through Joseph's first movement of mercy.
God names Himself healer and meets the reader in embodied need.
Provision arrives on the mountain where surrender felt most costly.
Mercy leads the rescued forward instead of only describing where they have been.
The Father gives grief room to breathe, adding emotional honesty to the visual book.
The name I AM steadies the reader at the threshold of the Son's movement.
Jesus names and claims His people before heaven, making discipleship personal.
The call to take up the cross keeps the visual devotional from becoming shallow inspiration.
Christ's patient knock creates an intimate scene of invitation and response.
Peter's courage waits for Jesus to say come before stepping onto impossible water.
Compassion for the crowd reveals how Jesus sees need before demanding strength.
The hand and voice of Jesus answer fear with nearness.
Jesus walks into the storm in the dark, an ideal hinge from depths into wonder.
Seventy-times-seven forgiveness makes Christ's kingdom practical and costly.
Jesus immediately reaches for the sinking disciple rather than watching from safety.
Resurrection hope stretches beyond the categories that once contained the reader.
God's breath entering dust is the clearest opening image for the Spirit's movement.
The Spirit rests on many shoulders, replacing isolated striving with shared strength.
Visible fruit keeps spiritual experience accountable to transformed living.
Moses' wish that all God's people receive the Spirit widens the invitation.
The Spirit fills a craftsperson's hands, honoring faithful work as sacred.
Jesus calls the disciples near before giving power, keeping witness rooted in relationship.
The listening ear makes room for the Spirit's present-tense guidance.
The hovering Spirit brings hope to places that do not yet have shape.
Another heart embodies renewal as more than a temporary emotional lift.
God speaks peace before sending, closing the trilogy selections with calm courage.
A new culmination gathers the Father's family, Christ's immeasurable love, and the Spirit's inner strengthening into the fullness of God.
